question.text: Priya invests Rs.2,00,000 in a mutual fund scheme with NAV of Rs.50. After stamp duty deduction, how many units will she receive?

explanation.text: The Logic: Stamp duty on new mutual fund investments is levied at 0.005%. On Rs.2,00,000, the stamp duty is Rs.10, so the net investible amount is Rs.1,99,990. At an NAV of Rs.50, units allotted = Rs.1,99,990 / Rs.50 = 3,999.8 (fractional units are permitted). The Trap: 4,000 units is the figure without stamp duty deduction. The stamp duty reduces the effective investment amount, resulting in slightly fewer units. Note: The allotment statement should clearly break down gross investment, stamp duty deducted, net investment, and units allotted.
